Laya eval-auto trial (catalog Entry 086, follow-up to PR #267). Cite #230 only. Catalog 70-75 HOLD. No Mark. Not a Feature GO.

You are in the worktree ~/DEVELOP/pfy-mentat/tmp/laya-trial on branch bot/laya-trial (based on origin/main 50d14ba). Work ONLY here. Never touch ~/DEVELOP/pfy-mentat (Mark's main checkout), its stashes, or other worktrees. No system installs, no sudo, no pip outside a venv.

Goal: head-to-head, measured comparison of Laya (https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya, `pip install "laya[serve]"`, CPU-only) against the current local CUA-S1-FORMS decision lane used by `./pfy decision` (scripts/pfy_jev_230.py), on the SAME decision cases, at the ~0.85 confidence gate. Read sources/entries/086-laya.md, docs/adr/0016-jev-decision-layer.md, docs/design/JEV-230-CUA-S1-FORMS-LOCK.md and examples/typed-decisions-local/ first.

Steps:
1. Create a venv at ~/DEVELOP/pfy-mentat/tmp/laya-trial/.venv-laya (gitignored; make sure it is never committed). Install CPU-only torch (use the PyTorch CPU index) and laya[serve]. HF weights cache under ~/DEVELOP/pfy-mentat/tmp/laya-trial/.hf-cache (set HF_HOME), also never committed.
2. Run `laya-serve` bound to 127.0.0.1 only. Verify the POST /v1/systemone wire contract against the ADR-0016 `typesafe` lane parser (use LAYA_JEV_STRICT if it exists); record any field drift. Point the typesafe lane's base URL at it only via an env var / flag for the trial, not by changing defaults.
3. Build a small labeled case set (aim 30-60 cases) from our real decision options: the live wizard/engine Choice options, data/decision-gates/push_hold.shadow.v0.json, docs/ops/human-decision-inventory.md. Labels must be ours, written down before running either model. Commit it as a data file.
4. Run both lanes on every case. Measure per lane: accuracy vs our labels, escalate rate at the 0.85 gate (confidence below gate means escalate), accuracy on the non-escalated cases, wrong-but-confident count (confidence >= 0.85 and wrong), p50/p95 latency (cold load separately from warm), and peak RSS RAM. Try both the base `laya` checkpoint and `laya-typed-decisions` if practical. Honest FAIL over stub success: if a lane can't run, record exactly why.
5. Write a reproducible trial script (e.g. scripts/ or examples/typed-decisions-local/), a machine-readable receipt under pipelines/ (JSON), and a results doc. Tests: one behavior-level test that the trial script fails closed (non-zero, clear reason) when the Laya venv/server is missing; no tautological unit sprawl. For each risk, say how it fails and how we recover.
6. Handoff doc in docs/ (e.g. docs/dogfood/LAYA-TRIAL-RESULTS.md) plus a dated entry in docs/PENDING-HANDOFF.md: what ran, the numbers, recommendation, open questions. Update sources/entries/086-laya.md status line with the nimo result. Do NOT change the default decision lane; any swap needs a measured win plus Mark's say, so at most recommend it.
7. Commit on bot/laya-trial with clear messages and `git push -u origin bot/laya-trial`. Do not open the PR yourself (gh is not logged in here); the org opens it. If push fails, leave commits local and say so in the handoff doc.
8. Stop laya-serve when done. Final output: a short summary with the head sha, the numbers table, and anything that failed.
